blocks.text: Essential Excel keyboard shortcuts for Mac clerks

Speed comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Excel for Mac has different shortcuts than the Windows version. If you find a shortcut is not working, check your System Settings under Keyboard > Shortcuts to see if macOS is claiming that command first.

items: Fn + F2: Edit the active cell content.
Shift + Space: Select the entire current row.
Ctrl + Space: Select the entire current column.
Cmd + D: Fill down the value from the cell above.
Cmd + T: Convert your current selection into a formatted table.

blocks.text: Data integrity is your primary responsibility. Excel often tries to be helpful by formatting numbers automatically. This leads to issues like losing leading zeros in IDs or phone numbers.
Set your column format to Text before you start typing IDs. Select the column, go to the Home tab, and change the Number Format dropdown to Text. This prevents Excel from stripping zeros.
blocks.title: Preserve leading zeros

blocks.text: Using Lazur to navigate Excel menus

When you are deep in a spreadsheet, digging through the ribbon menu slows you down. Lazur helps you find settings without breaking your focus. Hold Option + Command and ask where a feature is located. Lazur will draw a circle around the button on your screen.
Managing large datasets on a Mac

Excel can handle over one million rows, but performance drops if your sheet is messy. Keep your data in a proper table format. This makes formulas easier to read and allows for better filtering. Use Data Validation to restrict what can be typed into specific cells. This stops typos before they get saved.

items: Use Filter views to hide rows you do not need to see.
Freeze the top row so headers stay visible while you scroll.
Use conditional formatting to highlight duplicates in your list.
Remove empty rows to ensure your formulas calculate the full range.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my Excel files directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit cells for you. It points at the screen and explains how to perform tasks so you can do them yourself.

faq.question: How do I fix the leading zero problem in Excel?
faq.answer: Select the cells or columns, click the Number Format dropdown in the Home tab, and select Text. You can also use an apostrophe before the number to force text format.

faq.question: Why are my keyboard shortcuts not working?
faq.answer: macOS often overrides Excel shortcuts. Check your System Settings under Keyboard > Shortcuts to see if the key combination is used by the operating system.
